guard: a scope that settled FAILED still records its arm names, so a migration can walk it instead of hanging on it
why: THE PREVIOUS GUARD WAS VACUOUS ON THE CASE THAT MATTERED, and that is the lesson worth more
than the fix. `branch-missing.json` asks whether every RECORDED branch is present in the
migrated source. With NO branch recorded that question is vacuously true, so the guard passed
and the walk still entered nothing and still awaited `Promise.race([])`, which never settles.
A guard over an empty set grades nothing and is green forever. This is the second time in one
day that exact shape has been found in something this lane wrote.
WHY NO BRANCH WAS RECORDED. A successful scope records `result: { branches, value }`, and
`settle` writes `result` only when the status is `ok` -- result and error are exclusive, which
is correct and should stay that way. The consequence was not: a scope that FAILED recorded its
arm names NOWHERE, so a migration over an entirely UNEDITED program containing a failed race
hung. Not a bad diagnosis, not a wrong error: no answer at all. The names are not an outcome,
they are what the scope WAS, so they are a fact on the entry now.
WRITTEN ON THE FAILED PATH ONLY. The ok path already carries them inside `result`, and
duplicating a fact into two places is how the two come to disagree -- which is exactly the
defect this branch opened with, where a journal's keyed and ordered views disagreed about one
step.
TWO DIRECTIONS, and only one of them was a hang. `race` awaits `Promise.race([])` and waits
forever. `parallel` awaits `Promise.all([])`, which RESOLVES, so a failed parallel handed back
the recorded error having walked nothing at all -- an edit inside the failing arm was silent
rather than loud. The silent direction is the more dangerous one and it is graded here.
THE BACKSTOP IS NOT BELT AND BRACES. Journals already written carry no arm names and never
will, so the walk genuinely has nothing to enter for them. Refusing by name is the only honest
ending available; hanging is not one. Its message is deliberately its own, because "a recorded
branch is not in the source" is FALSE for that case -- nothing was recorded, and printing an
empty `missing:` list would send a reader hunting through their source for an arm that never
existed.
EVERY CELL IS WRAPPED IN ITS OWN DEADLINE, as in section 5 and for the same reason: a guard
against a HANG asserted by a bare `await` fails by hanging the suite, which scores as a timeout
rather than a red, and a mutation removing the guard would then be graded on the harness's
patience instead of on the code.
SPECIFIER BOUNDARY: not applicable, and checked rather than assumed. This suite imports
`../src/*.js` by relative path and the command is bare `tsx` with no build step, so the bytes
mutated are the bytes the suite loads.
ONE MUTATION SURVIVED THE FIRST RUN AND THE FIXTURE WAS AT FAULT, fixed on the test side. The
narrowness cell used `race({})`, which hangs on a LIVE run for the same `Promise.race([])` reason
-- so the cell timed out whether or not the code was mutated and could not see the difference. A
fixture that fails identically in both worlds is not a control. `parallel({})` resolves, so it is
the shape that can answer, and the fixture is a legacy entry walked against it: nothing recorded
AND nothing in the source, which is the only pair that separates the record from the source.
MEASURED AND NOT FIXED, named rather than left for someone else to rediscover: `await race({}, …)`
hangs on an ORDINARY run, no migration involved, because an empty arm set awaits
`Promise.race([])`. That is a program-authoring footgun in the same family and it is outside this
change, which is about what a walk does with a RECORD.

mutations.name: a failed settle stops recording the arm names, which is the shipped state before this fix
mutations.expectRed: so the arm names are recorded as a FACT on the entry instead
mutations.cell: so the arm names are recorded as a FACT on the entry instead
mutations.note: The exact shipped state that hung. It reddens at the entry rather than at the walk, which is where the defect actually is: everything downstream was reasoning correctly about a record that did not contain the answer.

mutations.name: the walk reads only `result` and ignores the fact, so a failed scope still looks armless
mutations.expectRed: and what it returns is the failure the run recorded, because it entered the arm that failed
mutations.cell: and what it returns is the failure the run recorded, because it entered the arm that failed
mutations.note: Half the fix without the other half: the entry now carries the names and nothing reads them. It does NOT redden the no-hang cell, because the backstop catches it and refuses -- so the mutation is graded on the cell that says WHAT the walk returned, not on the one that says it returned at all. Two cells that would collapse into one if either half were dropped.

mutations.name: the empty-set backstop is removed, so a journal written before the fix hangs again
mutations.expectRed: a journal written before the fix refuses rather than hanging
mutations.cell: a journal written before the fix refuses rather than hanging
mutations.note: The half that covers records nobody can go back and rewrite. Without it, every run recorded before this change is permanently un-migratable by hanging rather than by refusing, which is the difference between a bad answer and no answer.

mutations.name: PARANOID: the backstop stops checking the SOURCE, so an emptied scope is refused too
mutations.expectRed: an emptied scope over a record with no arm names is NOT caught by the backstop
mutations.cell: an emptied scope over a record with no arm names is NOT caught by the backstop
mutations.note: The other direction, and the one a fix written from the bug report alone lands on. The backstop's subject is a RECORD that carries no arm names, not a SOURCE that declares none. It first SURVIVED against a `race({})` fixture, and the reason is worth keeping: an empty `race` awaits `Promise.race([])` and hangs on a LIVE run too, so the cell timed out in both worlds and graded nothing. `parallel` resolves on an empty arm set, which is what makes the distinction observable at all.
